column2: but stacked block device drivers can and usually do change bi_bdev

column1: when sending on the bio to a lower device.  This can happen e.g. with the
nvme-multipath driver when a NVMe SSD sets the shared namespace bit.

as it is only passed to btrfs_rmap_block
column2: which uses it to pick the

column1: mapping to report if there are multiple reverse mappings.  As zone
writes can only do simple non-mirror writes right now
more complex will use the stripe tree there is no chance of the multiple
mappings case actually happening.

btrfs_record_physical_zoned
column2: which also removes a memory allocation and
